sentences.text:
By way of filing this criminal revision petition challenge has been made to the judgment dated
13.12.2004 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge & Special Judge, Sc/St (Prevention of
Atrocities) Act Cases, Pratapgarh in Criminal Appeal No.31/2004, whereby the learned appellate
court has affirmed the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 05.02.2004 passed by
the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Pratapgarh in Criminal Regular Case No.121/1997,
whereby the petitioner has been convicted for the offence under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food
Adulteration Act and sentenced to suffer one year's of simple imprisonment along with fine of Rs.
2,000/- and in default of payment of fine, to further undergo three months' simple imprisonment.

2. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that he will not assail conviction of the petitioner and confine his arguments to the alternative prayer of reduction of the sentence [2023:RJ-JD:41903] (2 of 3) [CRLR-943/2004] awarded by the trial court.
He submits that the incident in the present case pertains to the year 1997 and the present criminal revision is pending since the year 2004.
The petitioner has already suffered agony of protracted trial.
No fruitful purpose would be served by sending the present petitioner to jail at this stage.
With these submissions, learned counsel prays that by taking a lenient view, the sentence awarded to the petitioner may be reduced to the period already undergone by him.

Learned public prosecutor opposes the same but does not refute the fact that the petitioner has remained behind the bars for some time and the case is pending since long.

4. Since the revision petition against conviction is not pressed and after perusing the material,
nothing is noticed which requires interference in the finding of guilt reached by learned trial court and affirmed by the appellate court, this court does not wish to interfere in the judgment of conviction.
Accordingly, the judgment of conviction is maintained.

5. This Court in view of the judicial pronouncements made by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of Panchram vs The State Of Chhattisgarh and Ors. reported in AIR 2023 SC 1801 and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, age of petitioner, his status in the society and the fact that he faced financial hardship and had to go through mental agony, is of the view that ends of justice would be met, if sentence imposed upon him is reduced to the period already undergone by him.

entities.text: Panchram vs The State Of Chhattisgarh and Ors. reported in AIR 2023 SC 1801
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Accordingly, the judgment of conviction dated 05.02.2004 passed by the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Pratapbarh in Criminal Regular Case No.121/1997 as well as the [2023:RJ-JD:41903] (3 of 3) [CRLR-943/2004] judgment dated 13.12.2004 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Cases, Pratapgarh in Criminal Appeal No.31/2004 are affirmed but the quantum of sentence awarded by the learned trial court to the petitioner for his respective offences is modified to the extent that for each count, the sentence undergone by the petitioner till date would be sufficient and justifiable to serve the interest of justice.
The petitioner is on bail.
He need not surrender.
His bail bonds are discharged.
7. The revision petition is allowed.
Pending applications, if any, are disposed of.
Record be sent back.

(PRAVEER BHATNAGAR),J 26-AK Chouhan/-
